additional_info.body:
Hello,
Today 11 of March a client charged his vehicle between 4
:23:49 PM and 4:55:19 PM CU TIME but couldn't interrupt the charging session. When he attempted to stop charging he saw on the POS' screen "generic error 100".
We were able to stop the charging session only by rebooting the charger.
We also saw that on the Sifinity portal the charger is in status "Unavailable".
Can you please check the logs?
Thank you

additional_info.subject: ID0483786-DC/Si-D/IT-[Y2 / S1 313508370011] Check on Logs CRM:03097000508
additional_info.body:
Dear Rosita,
Thank you for contacting our eMobility Support, I hope this email finds you well.
Stop Attempt via POS:
At approximately 4:55 PM, the user attempted to terminate the session using the credit card terminal (POS). The terminal displayed
"Generic Error 100"
.
On screenshot we can see the end of the charging session.
The Meaning of "Error 100":
This specific error indicates a
communication timeout
between the payment terminal and the Management System (CSMS/Cloud). When a user presses "Stop" on the POS, the terminal sends a request to the payment provider to finalize the transaction. If the network signal is weak or if the backend takes too long to respond, the terminal "gives up" and shows this generic error.
Following the end of the session we see "
connection to a payment terminal never established"
Successful Termination via soft reboot:
Since the command via the physical terminal failed due to the timeout, the session remained active for a few more minutes. Our logs show that the session was finally closed successfully at
4:57:27 PM
through a command sent via the
soft reboot
. This command bypassed the POS communication loop and successfully unlocked the charger.
Conclusion
:
The charging process itself was successful, and the correct amount of energy was delivered. The "Error 100" was a localized communication failure at the terminal, which was resolved by the secondary stop command from your side "
Soft Reboot
"
I hope all the information shared could explain exactly what happened at the end of the session.
Apart from all the information shared, do you have any other questions or if I may proceed with closing this ticket?
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team – Felipe Moraes
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.

additional_info.subject: ID0483786-DC/Si-D/IT-[Y2 / S1 313508370011] Check on Logs CRM:03097000508
additional_info.body:
Hi Rosita ,
I hope this email finds you well.
Regarding this kind of disconnection in the charger, it usually occurs because of the internet signal in the OCPP router.
Checking the logs I don't see any information showing OCPP offline.
But if needed you can contact us in case you have any issue with charging sessions and we can check the signal in the OCPP router for you.
At the moment I suggest you active the outlets again and keep using the charger as normal because that issue doesn't makes the charger inoperative but can happens sometimes.
To check the route cause we need to have the charger being used and with this we can suggest a better way to avoid it happen again.
With best regar
ds,
eMobility Technical Support Team – Felipe Moraes
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.
